title: The Unsigned Ban
prompt: Wall Street can't buy another house. It keeps every one it has. Is that a ban, or the shape of one?
framing: On June 22 the Senate passed the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act 85–5; the House followed the next day 358–32. Tim Scott wrote the supply titles; Elizabeth Warren and Raphael Warnock wrote Title X: any for-profit entity with investment control of 350 or more single-family homes may not buy another. No divestiture — everything already owned stays owned. New construction, build-to-rent, renovation over 15%, and rent-to-own are exempt. The Treasury Secretary writes the regulations, with HUD and the SEC. The President neither signed nor vetoed it; the ten days ran out and it became law on July 11. Corporate landlords own more than 72,000 rentals in metro Atlanta — one in four — and the law does not touch one of them.

split.seam: radial (center vs rim, all four stations) — declared axis along y; radial is a candidate enum value, not ruled
split.rationale: Passage was 85–5, so the scalar runs along y: 'we passed it and the regs will handle it' vs 'they keep every house and the exemptions are the business model.' The centers sort weakly by y; the strong seam is between rings in every station — see zPattern.

zPattern.note: Second z-pattern on record; first with a POSITIVE shadow (+0.8) against an object at +0.2. All four rims negative — the rims did not follow the shadow. Candidate reading: rims converge on non-delivery whichever way the shadow points (the cynical-rim hypothesis). Seam is radial: every center sits 0.9–1.1 above its rim.

antiValentRationale: At the rim on both sides the statute is gone; what remains is who wrote the exemptions and why he would not sign it.

z.pos: The ban takes homes off Wall Street's table

fluid.text: It's in force. Title X is law as of July. What matters now is the rule Treasury writes, and we'll be reading every line of it.
fluid.zReason: It is law and the ban is in force today; enforcement is Treasury's and will be watched.

instrument.holder: Treasury, writing the regulations under Title X

coalition.text: Eighty-five to five. And he wouldn't put his name on it. So it lives or dies in the regulations, written by his Treasury.
coalition.zReason: Glad of the margins; uneasy that it needed no signature; the regs are the ballgame.

instrument.holder: Treasury and HUD — the regs, not the statute

denominated.text: He let it pass without signing so Bessent can gut it in the rule. Build-to-rent, new construction — those carve-outs were written by the people they carve out. It looks like a ban.
denominated.zReason: Let through unsigned so the same Treasury can hollow it in the rule; the exemptions were the industry's; a ban in appearance.

instrument.holder: the same Treasury that will hollow it in the rule

fluid.text: The supply titles are the bill. The cap is marginal — but it's real. As of July the big buyers are out of the resale market, and that's a fact on the ground.
fluid.zReason: The supply titles are the win; the cap is marginal but real — 350-plus buyers are out of the resale market as of July.

instrument.holder: the statute as passed — the supply titles

coalition.text: I voted for the supply. The cap I could take or leave — it's a line in the sand, and the market will walk around it.
coalition.zReason: Voted for the supply; the cap is a line the market will route around.

instrument.holder: the market, which routes around the cap

denominated.text: Telling an American company it can't buy a house is un-American. It's Warren's trophy. It'll be litigated, read narrowly, and do nothing. Good.
denominated.zReason: Regulating who may buy a house is un-American; it's Warren's; it will be litigated and read narrowly and do nothing — which is fine.

instrument.holder: Warren's Title X, headed for litigation

fluid.text: They already own the block. Banning them from buying more is banning the past. Make them sell — that would have been a law.
fluid.zReason: A ban on buying more, when they already own the block, is a ban on the past; divestiture would have been the thing.

instrument.holder: Congress, which banned the future and left the past

coalition.text: It's better than nothing, which is apparently the bar now. The rule's going to be written for the landlords. I'd love to be wrong.
coalition.zReason: Better than nothing, which is the standard now; expects the rule to be written for the landlords.

instrument.holder: Treasury, expected to write the rule for the landlords

denominated.text: Blackstone wrote the number. Build-to-rent is the loophole they'll drive the whole business through. And he didn't sign it — that's the tell. Nothing changes.
denominated.zReason: Blackstone wrote the 350 number and the build-to-rent carve-out; nothing changes; the unsigned law is the tell.

fluid.text: Good. BlackRock can't buy your neighbor's house anymore. Now enforce it.
fluid.zReason: Good: Wall Street can't buy your neighbor's house anymore; now enforce it.

instrument.holder: the law, now in force — Wall Street can't buy your neighbor's house

coalition.text: I'll believe it when I see one of their trucks leave a street. And somebody tell me why he didn't sign it.
coalition.zReason: Will believe it when a truck leaves; and why didn't he sign it?

instrument.holder: a President who wouldn't sign it and a Treasury that hasn't enforced it

denominated.text: They passed a 'ban' that lets them keep every house and build ten thousand more to rent. The uniparty protecting BlackRock. And he wouldn't even touch it.
denominated.zReason: A "ban" that lets them keep everything and keep building rentals — the uniparty protecting BlackRock, and Trump wouldn't touch it.

LF.text: The left reads the statute as in force and the rule as the object: a ban whose reach is now an executive act by the executive that would not sign it.

LC.text: The left is glad of eighty-five votes and cannot stop looking at the missing signature.

LD.text: The left has decided the exemptions were dictated and the unsigned law is the receipt, and in saying so concedes the ban is real enough to need hollowing.

RF.text: The right's institutions count the cap as marginal and real and move on to the supply titles, which they wrote.

RC.text: The right voted for the bill and will let the market walk around the one line in it that it did not want.

RD.text: The right's rim has two enemies for one law — Warren for writing it and the uniparty for gutting it — and has stopped asking which it believes.
